stem: A payment API has steady relational baseline traffic plus periodic spikes and wants lower idle overprovisioning while keeping managed relational operations.

choices.text: Use Aurora Serverless v2 with a bounded ACU range for elasticity.
Use Aurora provisioned capacity sized for peak demand at all times.
Use DynamoDB on-demand as a drop-in relational replacement for SQL joins.
Use fixed provisioned relational instances and schedule manual resize windows.

rationale: Aurora Serverless v2 aligns with variable relational demand by scaling compute within configured bounds. Peak-sized provisioned clusters can carry idle cost between spikes. DynamoDB on-demand is a different data model and not a drop-in relational SQL-join replacement. Manual resize windows add operational overhead and can miss unexpected spikes.
